docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Terms are Sanskrit unless marked (Pa. = Pali, Pk. = Prakrit, Ar. = Arabic, Pe. = Persian, Pu. = Punjabi, Ta. = Tamil, Be. = Bengali, Gu. = Gujarati, Hi. = Hindi, Ur. = Urdu).

Term Meaning adhyāsa Superimposition; in Advaita, the mistaking of the non-self for the self Advaita “Non-duality”; the Vedānta of Śaṅkara, holding that Brahman alone is ultimately real ahiṃsā Non-injury, non-violence ajātivāda “Non-origination”; Gauḍapāda’s doctrine that nothing is ever really born aloka In Jain cosmology, the infinite empty space beyond the occupied universe anātman “Not-self”; the Buddhist teaching that no permanent self is found in the constituents of a person (Pali anattā) anattā (Pa.) See anātman anekāntavāda The Jain doctrine of the many-sidedness of reality ānvīkṣikī “Investigation”; the science of reasoning, in the Arthaśāstra and later āpaddharma The rules permitted in times of distress aṟam (Ta.) Virtue, dharma; the first book of the Tirukkuṟaḷ artha Wealth, power, material well-being; one of the aims of life āryikā A Digambara Jain nun asaṃkhyāta “Innumerable”; in Jain mathematics, a class of numbers between the countable and the infinite āsana A posture; in the Yogasūtra, a steady seat for meditation āśrama A stage or mode of life: student, householder, forest-dweller, renouncer Ati-Śūdra “Below (or beyond) the Śūdras”; an older term, made central by Phule, for the castes treated as untouchable ātman The self avadhāna “Attention”; public feats of memory and simultaneous attention, such as the young Śrīmad Rājacandra performed avatāra “Descent”; an incarnation of a deity, especially of Viṣṇu avidyā Ignorance; in Advaita, the cause of the appearance of multiplicity Āyurveda “Knowledge of life”; the classical Indian system of medicine Bahujan (Hi.) “The many”; in modern anti-caste usage, the non-elite majority of lower castes Bāul (Be.) A wandering devotional singer of Bengal bhakti Devotion to a personal deity bhavacakra The Buddhist “wheel of becoming” depicting the realms of rebirth bhikkhunī (Pa.) A fully ordained Buddhist nun bidʿa (Ar.) “Innovation”; a practice without warrant in the Qurʾān and the Prophet’s example, condemned by reformers bodhisattva One who seeks awakening for the sake of all beings Brahman In the Upaniṣads and Vedānta, the ultimate reality brahmāṇḍa “Egg of Brahmā”; a world-system in Purāṇic cosmology cakra “Wheel”; a centre in the subtle body in yogic and tantric texts cakravartin “Wheel-turner”; the ideal universal monarch cetanā (Pa.) Intention; identified by the Buddha with karma cuyamariyātai (Ta.) Self-respect; the ideal and the name of Periyar’s movement daṇḍa Punishment; the coercive power of the king dargāh (Pe.) The shrine and tomb of a Sufi saint darśana “View”; a philosophical system; also the seeing of a deity or holy person dhammasattha (Pa.) A law book of the Theravāda kingdoms of Southeast Asia dharma Law, duty, right order; the Buddha’s teaching; in Jainism also the medium of motion dharmasaṅkaṭa A conflict of duties dhvani Suggestion; in poetics, meaning conveyed without being stated dhyāna Meditation; meditative absorption (Pa. jhāna) Digambara “Sky-clad”; the Jain tradition whose monks go naked doṣa “Fault”; in Āyurveda, one of the three bodily principles, vāta, pitta and kapha dravya Substance; in Jainism, the six constituents of the universe Dvaita “Dualism”; the Vedānta of Madhva ekaśaraṇa “Refuge in the One”; the devotional order of Śaṅkaradeva in Assam fatwā (Ar.) A legal opinion given by a qualified scholar in answer to a question gharānā (Hi.) A lineage or school of Hindustani musicians guṇa In Sāṃkhya, the three constituents of matter: sattva, rajas, tamas guṇasthāna In Jainism, one of the fourteen stages of spiritual progress ḥākimiyya (Ar.) Sovereignty; in Mawdūdī’s thought, the exclusive sovereignty of God over law and the state haṭhayoga The “yoga of force”, using postures, breath control and seals hukam (Pu.) The divine order or command, in Sikh teaching ijtihād (Ar.) Independent reasoning from the sources of Islamic law jāti Birth-group; caste as an endogamous, often occupational community jīva A living being or soul jyotiṣa The science of the luminaries: astronomy, calendrics and astrology kaivalya “Isolation”; the goal of Sāṃkhya and of Patañjali’s yoga kalpa An aeon; in the Purāṇas, a day of Brahmā kāma Desire, pleasure, love; one of the aims of life karma Action, and its consequences for the agent khālsā (Pu.) The community of initiated Sikhs founded by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699 khudī (Pe.) Selfhood; the central concept of Iqbal’s philosophy kṣaṇikavāda The Buddhist doctrine of momentariness laṅgar (Pu.) The Sikh community kitchen open to all loka A world or realm of existence lokapuruṣa The Jain universe imagined as a giant human figure madrasa (Ar.) A school of Islamic learning mahāvākya “Great sentence”; an Upaniṣadic statement of the identity of self and Brahman mahāyuga The great cycle of four ages (4,320,000 years in the Purāṇic reckoning) manvantara The period of one Manu; 71 mahāyugas maʿqūlāt (Ar.) The “rational” sciences of the madrasa curriculum, as against the transmitted sciences (manqūlāt) maṭha A monastery, especially of Hindu renouncers māyā Illusion, or the creative power that makes the world appear Meru The cosmic mountain at the centre of the world in Hindu, Buddhist and Jain cosmology mettā (Pa.) Loving-kindness millat (Ar.) A community of faith; distinguished by Ḥusain Aḥmad Madanī from the territorial nation (qaum) mīrī–pīrī (Pu.) Temporal and spiritual authority, symbolised by Guru Hargobind’s two swords mokṣa Liberation from the round of rebirth nafs (Ar.) The self or soul; in Sufism, the lower self to be disciplined nām (Pu.) The divine name, on which Sikhs meditate Navya-Nyāya The “new reason”; the logic and epistemology founded by Gaṅgeśa nēcharī (Ur.) “Naturalist”; a nickname for the followers of Sayyid Ahmad Khan nidāna A link in the Buddhist chain of dependent origination nirguṇa “Without qualities”; of the divine, beyond all attributes nirvāṇa “Blowing out”; the Buddhist goal, the cessation of craving and rebirth niścaya-naya In Jain thought, the ultimate standpoint, from which the pure soul is untouched by karma pañcāṅga The traditional almanac with its “five limbs” pāñjrāpoḷ (Gu.) A Jain refuge and hospital for animals pativratā A wife vowed to her husband; the ideal of wifely devotion in the epics and law-books pīr (Pe.) A Sufi master or saint prakṛti Primordial matter; in Āyurveda, a person’s constitution pralaya The dissolution of the world at the end of a cosmic period pramā A true cognition, the product of a means of knowledge (pramāṇa) pramāṇa A valid means of knowledge prasthānatraya The “three foundations” of Vedānta: Upaniṣads, Gītā, Brahmasūtra pratītyasamutpāda Dependent origination prekṣā dhyāna “Meditation of perception”; a system of meditation developed in the Terāpanthī Jain order from the 1970s puruṣa Person; in Sāṃkhya, the conscious self puruṣārtha An aim of human life: dharma, artha, kāma, mokṣa puṣṭimārga “Path of grace”; the devotional tradition of Vallabha qaum (Ur.) A people or nation qawwālī (Ur.) Devotional song performed at Sufi shrines rāga A melodic framework of Indian classical music rahit (Pu.) The code of conduct of the Khālsā, codified in the Sikh Rahit Maryādā rājadharma The duties of a king rasa “Taste” or “relish”; aesthetic emotion ṛta Cosmic and moral order in the Ṛgveda rūḥ (Ar.) Spirit śābdabodha Verbal cognition; the understanding produced by a sentence, as analysed by the grammarians, Mīmāṃsakas and Naiyāyikas sāgaropama “Ocean-measure”; a Jain unit of immense time sahajdhārī (Pu.) A Sikh who has not taken Khālsā initiation and does not keep uncut hair sallekhanā The Jain practice of fasting unto death at the end of life samanvaya Coherent connection; harmonious reading; in modern usage, synthesis or harmony saṃnyāsa Renunciation; the life of the renouncer (saṃnyāsin) saṃsāra The round of rebirth saṃskāra A latent impression left by action or experience; also a life-cycle rite saṃvāda Dialogue; the title of the record of a dialogue between pandits and philosophers held at Pune in 1983 saṅkalpa A ritual statement of intention sant A devotional poet of the late medieval period, especially of the nirguṇa tradition śānta The “tranquil” rasa, admitted by Abhinavagupta and others sarnā The sacred grove of the Munda, Oraon and other Adivasi communities of Jharkhand; hence Sarna, a name for their religion śāstra A treatise; authoritative teaching on a subject sattra In Assam, a monastery and centre of devotion and performance of Śaṅkaradeva’s order satya Truth satyāgraha “Holding firmly to truth”; Gandhi’s method of non-violent resistance śramaṇa A renouncer outside the Vedic fold, such as the Buddhists, Jains and Ājīvikas śuddhi “Purification”; the Arya Samaj rite for admitting or readmitting converts to Hinduism ṣulḥ-i kull (Pe.) “Peace with all”; Akbar’s policy towards religious communities svadharma One’s own duty Śvetāmbara “White-clad”; the Jain tradition whose monks and nuns wear white tāla A rhythmic cycle in Indian music taqlīd (Ar.) “Imitation”; adherence to the rulings of an established school of law Tat Khālsā (Pu.) “The true Khālsā”; the Singh Sabha reformers who insisted on a distinct Sikh identity tattva A principle or constituent of reality tiṇai (Ta.) A poetic landscape in classical Tamil poetics tīrthaṅkara “Ford-maker”; one of the twenty-four teachers of the Jain path in each half-cycle trivarga The triad of aims: dharma, artha and kāma ʿulamāʾ (Ar.) Scholars of Islamic law and theology utsarpiṇī, avasarpiṇī The ascending and descending half-cycles of Jain time vāda Debate; in Nyāya, honest debate aimed at truth varṇa One of the four classes of Brahmanical theory vipassanā (Pa.) Insight meditation Viśiṣṭādvaita “Qualified non-dualism”; the Vedānta of Rāmānuja vyāpti “Pervasion”; the invariable concomitance on which an inference rests vyavahāra-naya In Jain thought, the conventional standpoint, from which the soul acts and is bound waḥdat al-wujūd (Ar.) “Unity of being”; the metaphysics associated with Ibn ʿArabī yama, niyama The restraints and observances, first limbs of Patañjali’s yoga yuga One of the four ages: Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, Kali zīj (Pe.) A set of astronomical tables in the Islamic tradition
